title: Slow and steady
hook: You don't have to do everything this week. Here's what matters now, and what can wait.

screens.text: A week in, a lot of new Muslims hit the same wall: *there's so much.* Prayers, Arabic, food, clothes, advice from everyone. Today you'll sort it out: what's required now, and what can wait.
**The religion is easy.** The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever makes the religion too heavy on themselves gets worn down by it. Aim for what's right, get close to it, and take heart [Bukhari 39].
bubbles: He also said the deeds Allah loves most are the **regular** ones, even if they're small [Bukhari 6464]. Steady beats intense.

screens.text: **Islam came in stages.** The early revelations were about faith in Allah. Rules on what's allowed and forbidden came once hearts had settled [Bukhari 4993]. When the Prophet ﷺ sent a teacher to Yemen, he gave him an order to teach in [Bukhari 1395].

screens.prompt: What did he tell the teacher to teach first? Put them in order.
screens.feedback: Belief, then prayer, then charity. Your duties don't shrink, but your learning can go one step at a time.

screens.prompt: Which of these are required of you right now? Select all that apply.

options.text: Praying all five prayers, with what you know so far
options.feedback: Yes. All five are due from day one, said with what you know. It grows daily.

options.text: Avoiding pork and alcohol
options.feedback: Yes. These are clear limits from day one. Struggling with one isn't the same as rejecting it.

options.text: Being kind to your parents
options.feedback: Yes. Required, even when they disagree with you (Day 4).

options.text: Memorizing a long chapter of the Qur'an
options.feedback: Not yet. Al-Fatiha is your goal for now. More Qur'an is great, at your own pace.

options.text: Praying extra sunnah prayers every day
options.feedback: Not required. Sunnah prayers are a beautiful extra. Day 57 introduces them.

options.text: Taking an Arabic name and new clothes
options.feedback: Not required. Keep your name unless its meaning is bad, and any modest clothes work (Day 9).

screens.title: The rule of thumb: keep the basics steady, and add extras slowly

points.text: Extra prayers, extra fasts, hours of study every night. It feels great, for a while.

points.label: Week six: the wall
points.text: Converts who try to do everything in week two often burn out by week six [Field Guide ch. 9].

points.label: A hard week
points.text: Don't drop to nothing. All five are still due: pray each one with what you know so far, and let the extras rest.

points.label: Steady
points.text: Keep the basics steady and add extras slowly. Small and regular is what Allah loves most [Bukhari 6464].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- The religion is easy; overburdening yourself leads to being overcome [Bukhari 39]. The most beloved deeds are the regular ones, even if small [Bukhari 6464].
- Revelation and teaching came in stages: belief first, then prayer, then zakat [Bukhari 1395; Bukhari 4993; IslamQA 109201]. Gradualism applies to **teaching order**, not to cancelling obligations: all five prayers are due from day one [IslamWeb 529861; SeekersGuidance 167692].
- A convert's knowledge is "a marathon, not a sprint" [SeekersGuidance, recent convert]. Converts who take on every extra at once often burn out [Field Guide ch. 9].
- **Witr (Hanafi):** wajib; 3 rak'ahs with one salam, like Maghrib (sit after two for the shahada/tashahhud, stand for the third); prayed after Isha until dawn; in the third rak'ah, after recitation, a takbir with raised hands, then the qunut du'a, then ruku'. One rak'ah alone isn't valid in the Hanafi school [SeekersGuidance, witr; First Instructions on Worship; Qibla 36911]. Unlike Maghrib, Hanafi witr has al-Fatiha and a surah in all three rak'ahs; for a learner, that means saying what they know in each standing, as in any rak'ah. Until the qunut is learned (Day 57), a short du'a stands in for it. Other schools: strongly recommended sunnah, often 2 + 1 or 1. `Q18`

**Likely questions**
- *"What's required this month?"* Belief; five prayers with wudu (and ghusl when needed); avoid clear haram (pork, alcohol, zina, etc.); kindness to parents; witr (Hanafi). Fasting when Ramadan comes. Everything else can wait.
- *"Someone said music/X is haram."* Some things are clear, some are differences of opinion (Q22). Don't overload; suggest asking the imam, and note that many people present opinions as rules.
- *"I keep missing Fajr."* Gentle: pray it as soon as you wake; alarms, earlier sleep; Day 21 covers making up. Missing isn't the end.
- *"How do I pray witr?"* Walk through the masjid variant step by step.
- *"I can't remember the witr du'a."* Any short du'a for now; the full qunut comes on Day 57.

**Escalate:** someone doing so much they're not sleeping or eating, or showing signs of anxiety or scrupulosity (offer care, mentor); anyone who has stopped praying altogether (warmly, mentor).

**Don't**
- Don't say "start with one or two prayers" or "build up to five" (Q4).
- Don't make witr sound as big as the five, and don't teach the full qunut here.
- Don't hand them a long list of new rules. This lesson is about lightening the load.
madhabNote: Witr: in the Hanafi school it's wajib (just below the five), always 3 rak'ahs with one salam, with the qunut du'a before bowing in the third. In the Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools it's a strongly recommended sunnah, commonly prayed as 2 rak'ahs, a salam, then 1 more; a single rak'ah is valid for them. All agree it's prayed after Isha and before dawn.
